newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka plans to sell 35 pct stake in Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans to sell 35 pct stake in Telecom.

text.p: Sri Lanka plans to sell a 35 percent stake in state-owned Sri Lanka Telecom (SLT) to a strategic investor, officials in charge of the government's privatisation programme said on Thursday.

"Advertisements will go out locally and internationally within a week, calling for a strategic partner to take up a 35 percent stake and management in Sri Lanka Telecom," said an official of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC).
"An information memorandum can now be made available at the discretion of the government to any interested party who is an experienced telecommunications operator," the official said.
The planned sale was recommended by a consortium which was commissioned to find a way to restructure the state telecommunications company, he said.
A consortium was assembled in April with a mandate to identify a strategic partner.
The consortium involves Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Deloitte Touche Tomatsu International, Slaughter & May and Development Finance Corp of Ceylon (DFCC).
"Coming this far in a matter of five months is rapid progress by any standards," said Maxi Prelis, general manager of DFCC which coordinated the project in Colombo.
